title: Mid-latitude afforestation shifts general circulation and tropical precipitation

settings.description: NCAR CAM 3.0-CLM 3.5-CASA' with an interactive carbon cycle and an interactive slab ocean holding lateral ocean heat transport fixed, run to equilibrium.
The control run with present-day vegetation distribution.
The TREE experiment converting all C3 grass and agriculture between 30 N and 60 N to broad-leaf deciduous trees, totalling 18 million km2 or 19.2 per cent of the surface area in that band.
Additional sensitivity studies converting only agricultural land to forest.
Afforested locations where the water supply gap index 1 - ET/PET widens, meaning the surface cannot meet atmospheric evaporative demand.
Afforested locations with abundant soil moisture where the water supply gap narrows.
The June-August season, over which the water supply gap and the surface energy terms are evaluated.
The 30 N to 60 N band, where the conversion is imposed and the local energy and water budgets are reported.
Boreal regions north of 60 N, reported separately for the below-ground carbon response.
The southern edge of the Amazon forest, where the precipitation maximum shifts away.
The Sahara and upper Sahel, where precipitation increases.
Tropical and unmodified mid-latitude regions, reported separately in the carbon accounting.
Equilibrium accounting combining terrestrial uptake with the compensating oceanic CO2 release of 60 to 85 per cent.

claims.to: absorbed solar radiation at the surface
claims.statement: Afforestation darkens the surface, and the primary change in the surface energy budget is an increase in absorbed solar radiation.

claims.from: increased absorbed solar radiation at the surface
claims.statement: The increased absorbed solar radiation raises near-surface air temperatures north of 30 N.

claims.from: the albedo difference between grasses and trees
claims.statement: The albedo difference is evident in all seasons, showing it is not entirely due to snow masking by trees but to the specified grass-tree albedo contrast.
claims.match_note: Not extracted, so the snow-masking alternative is not ruled out in the graph.

claims.statement: Albedo also changes over the ocean through a decrease in summer sea ice area, adding to the absorbed solar anomaly.
Cloud radiative forcing acts as a weak positive feedback, adding 0.44 W/m2 to the net incoming radiation, about 9 per cent of the vegetation-driven change.
Cloud cover decreases by 2 per cent at all vertical levels and by 4.5 per cent at low levels, with three quarters of the forcing shortwave and one quarter longwave.

claims.to: Northern Hemisphere mid-latitude annual mean temperature
claims.statement: Northern Hemisphere mid-latitude temperature rises by 0.93 C in the annual mean at equilibrium.
Water vapour increases by 6.9 per cent over Northern Hemisphere mid-latitudes, consistent with the Clausius-Clapeyron expectation of about 7 per cent per degree of warming.
The water vapour increase enhances downward longwave radiation at the surface.
Precipitation and evaporation both increase in the mid-latitudes but evaporation increases more, exporting 1.1 kg/s of water from the region.
Two thirds of the evaporation increase comes from land at 22.7 kg/s and one third from the ocean at 10.4 kg/s.
The water supply gap primarily widens in afforested regions during summer, indicating relatively drier conditions.

claims.to: afforestation-induced widening of the water supply gap
claims.statement: Total leaf area index is uncorrelated with the change in dryness measured by the widening water supply gap, at r = 0.07 and p = 0.12.
claims.match_note: Not extracted. A null result that guards against reading the drying as a vegetation-density effect.

claims.statement: Where the water supply gap widens the absorbed energy cannot leave as latent heat, so surface temperature rises by 0.62 C in the Northern Hemisphere annual mean and the energy leaves as sensible heat and longwave flux.

claims.from: abundant soil moisture in afforested areas
claims.to: the warming from enhanced solar absorption
claims.statement: In afforested areas with abundant soil moisture the enhanced latent heat loss can ameliorate the warming from enhanced solar absorption and net longwave radiation.
claims.match_note: Not extracted. This is the branch that decides whether afforestation warms, so its absence leaves the extracted warming chain unconditioned.

claims.from: widening versus narrowing water supply gap
claims.statement: Mid-latitude locations with a widening water supply gap warm 2 C more in summer than those with a narrowing gap, 3.5 C against 1.5 C for JJA.

claims.from: differences in soil moisture representation across models
claims.to: divergence in the simulated mid-latitude forest impact
claims.statement: The dependence of the warming response on soil moisture status may explain why models disagree on the impact of mid-latitude forests.
Afforestation shifts precipitation belts northward, particularly over the Pacific but also over the Atlantic and South America.
claims.match_note: Not extracted as its own record; only the two regional consequences were captured.

claims.to: northward atmospheric energy transport at the equator
claims.statement: Northward atmospheric energy transport at the equator falls from 1.21 PW by 0.17 PW, a 13 per cent reduction, confirming southward redistribution of the anomalous energy.

claims.from: northward shift of the Hadley circulation
claims.to: precipitation over the southern Amazon basin
claims.statement: The northward shift dries the southern edge of the Amazon forest.

claims.from: northward shift of the Hadley circulation
claims.to: precipitation over the Sahel and Sahara
claims.statement: The northward shift increases precipitation over the Sahara and upper Sahel.
The drying of the southern Amazon causes a decrease in productivity, showing that extratropical forest change affects tropical carbon cycling.

claims.from: increased precipitation over the Sahara and upper Sahel
claims.statement: The added water is released directly as ground evaporation under prescribed land cover, so no productivity increase and no carbon balance change occur.
claims.match_note: Not extracted. An asymmetry between the drying and wetting responses that a planner would need.

claims.from: conversion of grass and crops to forest
claims.statement: The land takes up 270 PgC across the afforested locations at equilibrium, 155 PgC above ground and 112 PgC below ground.
Boreal regions north of 60 N lose 28 PgC from below-ground carbon pools as higher temperatures accelerate decomposition.
A further 3 PgC is lost from unmodified mid-latitudes and 9 PgC from the tropics, leaving a net global biospheric sequestration of 228 PgC.

claims.from: net biospheric carbon uptake with compensating oceanic release
claims.to: atmospheric CO2 and global mean temperature
claims.statement: Atmospheric CO2 falls by 16-46 ppm, giving a global cooling of 0.2 to 0.7 C.

claims.from: combined biogeophysical warming and biogeochemical cooling
claims.statement: Biogeophysical effects alone warm the globe by 0.3 C, and combined with the CO2 cooling the net global change is -0.4 to +0.1 C, so the two nearly cancel while regional impacts remain substantial.
claims.match_note: Not extracted. The paper's headline framing, that a near-zero global signal hides large regional effects, is absent from the graph.
